transcript: on my second day at the Edinburgh Fringe I saw Hold Onto Your Butts Flight Sh!t Theater Or What’s Left of Us Weather Girl and Patti Harrison's show entitled “My Huge Tits because they're infected not fake” hold on to your butts as you can probably tell is a Jurassic Park parody / comedic retelling so of course the fun of it is seeing them represent these big spectacle moments but through little props and low tech stagecraft it's just silly fun and it doesn't try to be anything more by the way though I would only recommend this to people who are familiar with the film Flight is a 20 minute immersive experience performed inside a shipping container made up to look like an airplane it's primarily an audio play but it does use other media and design elements to convey the story which has to do with parallel universes and there's like a Schroedinger’s cat metaphor the attempts to explore a philosophical theme felt a little bit forced to me I don't think it leaves as much of a meaningful impression as it's trying to but I did find it pretty thrilling and there's also a dark humor underneath it which is fun Sh!t Theater is the name of this performance art duo and this show is called Sh!t Theater or what's left of us the show is conceived around the ritual of communal folk singing so it's like one part folk sing along one part memoir about their experiences with a particular folk club that burnt down and also about the feeling of being personally and artistically lost in the wake of grief it's just a beautiful experience all around and it's infused with their offbeat sense of humor and their multi layered theatricality Weather Girl is by Brian Watkins who wrote a play that I thought was criminally underrated a few years ago at Lincoln Center so I'm happy to see that this has become one of the big hits of the festival this one is a fictional solo play about this titular weathergirl who is kind of having a breakdown while the wildfires rip through California The whole thing is kind of unsettling but also very funny as it's kind of highlighting the absurdity of denial and performed normalcy and there's even some like magical realist twists to it too I often talk about how I struggle with plays that are told mostly through narration but the content here is just filled with so much tension and intriguecand insight that it was a rare exception where I was completely engrossed having said that I do actually think this would have worked well as a traditionally dramatized play I mostly knew Patti Harrison from her film work this was my first exposure to her stand up and honestly I thought it was so brilliant it's kind of hard to describe without spoiling surprises but I will say it's very theatrical in the way that it's layering in fiction and reality keeping the audience on our toes and just going off in bizarre directions
